records.source_statement: Unnumbered heading 'Of the house of the Thiefe, and the mark thereof' begins this phase below an already indexed 'Which way the Thief is gone' discussion.
preconditions: New heading below the divider on printed page347.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not re-extract the printed passage above this heading from B02u.

records.source_statement: The sign containing the thief significator and its quarter of heaven are used to conjecture the town quarter of the stolen thing.
preconditions: Identify the actual thief significator in the question figure.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A historical location conjecture, not evidence of any real thief or object's position.

records.source_statement: If the thief significator is in the first, seventh, fourth or tenth angle, Lilly respectively assigns east, west, north or south; intermediate angles suggest intermediate directions.
preconditions: The relevant house is the thief significator's, not the Moon's.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The rule describes quarter-based conjecture without calibrated geography.

records.source_statement: Lilly assigns the Sun's (☉) place to the house the thief is in, and the Moon's (☽) place to the door of that house.
preconditions: Original PDF381/printed347 explicitly gives the place of Sun for the thief's house and the place of Moon for its door.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Image-first visual correction: the Sun glyph has an interior dot, not a Part-of-Fortune cross; this historical locational assertion has no verified outcome.

records.source_statement: If Sun (☉) is in an oriental sign, Lilly places the house in the eastern part relative to the master or the one who lost the goods.
preconditions: Sun, rather than an unspecified fortune-like point, is in an oriental sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The original is a claimed directional indication, not an independently surveyed dwelling.

records.source_statement: A separate heading 'The Door of the house' introduces house-entry position predictions.
preconditions: Located below the thief-house quarter section on printed347.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from identifying where stolen goods are kept.

records.source_statement: To describe which side of the house the doorway occupies, examine whether Moon lies in an angular, succedent or cadent part and the related source sign/quarter.
preconditions: Moon is the explicit subject and the sentence carries onto printed348.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Continuation spans the original page break. This row had a shifted original draft schema; the exact prior source bytes were frozen before mechanical repair.
Editorial source paraphrase only; no independently authenticated person or outcome.

records.source_statement: Moon in a fixed sign is said to signify a house with one main door.
preconditions: Fixed sign of Moon, not the thief significator.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original elsewhere gives other conditions for door count; do not declare measured certainty.

records.source_statement: Moon in movable sign is said to imply a doorway raised above earth, perhaps with another small door.
preconditions: Moon must be in movable sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The second small-door possibility is hedged in source.

records.source_statement: Saturn aspecting the relevant sign is said to indicate a door formerly broken and mended, or an old, dark/black door.
preconditions: Saturn must have the specified aspect to the Moon's sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The passage offers alternatives; not observed damage.

records.source_statement: Mars aspecting the relevant sign is said to show burn/fire marks around the entrance.
preconditions: Mars aspect relevant house-entry sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is an attributed historical sign, not a forensic burn assessment.

records.source_statement: Saturn and Mars in favourable aspect to the same sign are interpreted as a strong door of iron or mostly iron.
preconditions: Both planetary aspect connections are named in printed source.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not an independent construction-material report.

records.source_statement: An unfortunate Moon is said to mark a broken or spoiled gate/door.
preconditions: Moon actually under stated affliction.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No real building damage inferred.

records.source_statement: Moon with little light is claimed to show no main opening toward highway but a rear doorway.
preconditions: Weakly illuminated Moon under this source rule.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Door orientation not established by source mythology.

records.source_statement: The distinct heading 'Tokens of the Thiefs house' begins another set of door/gate clues.
preconditions: Unnumbered source heading on printed348.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not merge this list with preceding sign-count rule.

records.source_statement: Moon square, conjunct or opposite Mars is said to signify a door burned by fire/candle or cut by iron instrument.
preconditions: Specific adverse body/aspect between Moon and Mars.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Whether original glyph represents conjunction versus a different relationship must be checked visually.

records.source_statement: Moon trine or sextile Mars is said to signify a thief-house door mended with iron.
preconditions: Specifically favourable Moon–Mars aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source assigns same planet Mars to contrary door claims under different aspects.

records.source_statement: Moon newly gaining light is said to signify a doorway partially below earth/bank or approached by descending steps.
preconditions: New increase in Moon's illumination.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not substitute lunar waning or any Moon-in-house condition.

records.source_statement: In the later tokens list, Moon in fixed or movable sign implies one outward door, while Moon in common sign implies more than one.
preconditions: The classification is sign mode of Moon in this subsection.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This repeats/qualifies earlier single-door claim; not a separate observed property.

records.source_statement: With Moon in a fixed sign, an original Taurus-like glyph is linked to an underground gate and Aquarius-like glyph to a house on a bank side.
preconditions: Original named fixed sign glyphs ♉ and ♒ must be checked against image.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Illustrative site hypotheses, not externally verified.

records.source_statement: Moon in movable sign can signify a gate higher than ground and ascending a step to enter.
preconditions: Moon in movable sign, separate from the other movable door rule.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source includes personal 'probatum est' claim, not independently audited observation.

records.source_statement: Unfortunate Moon signifies broken gate; the Moon's quarter of heaven is additionally assigned to the door's side.
preconditions: Moon must be unfortunate for breakage and separately located by quarter for direction.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Breakage and compass orientation are distinct condition branches.

records.source_statement: Saturn in conjunction/square/opposition to Moon suggests broken, old or black door; favourable sextile/trine suggests it has been repaired.
preconditions: Distinguish Saturn's hard and soft aspects to Moon.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This overlaps earlier Saturn-to-sign rule, preserve source two formulations separately.

records.source_statement: Another distinct heading asks where the thief remains or dwells.
preconditions: Printed p348 bottom, continues on p349.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not a separate observed residential address.

records.source_statement: The thief's significator sign and celestial quarter allegedly determine that quarter of town where the goods/person are situated.
preconditions: A significator and its zodiacal quarter are identified.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Continuation spans the original page break. This row had a shifted original draft schema; the exact prior source bytes were frozen before mechanical repair.
Editorial source paraphrase only; no independently authenticated person or outcome.

records.source_statement: Moon eastern versus western quarter allegedly marks the house gate on east versus west side.
preconditions: Moon's actual quarter, not fixed/movable sign mode.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from thief's significator locational quarter.

records.source_statement: Moon fixed sign is claimed to indicate a single ground-level door in the thief's dwelling.
preconditions: Moon fixed sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not assume same as p348's separate sun/mars aspects.

records.source_statement: Moon movable sign is claimed to indicate a door raised some steps from ground.
preconditions: Moon movable sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Repeats the entrance suggestion within a new locational method.

records.source_statement: Saturn aspecting the relevant sign is used to infer age/breakage/blackness; Mars likewise alleged to increase cracks or repair needs.
preconditions: Both effects depend on which planetary significator regards the Moon sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No physical inspection; claims may conflict with favourable aspects elsewhere.

records.source_statement: When Moon has little light during those adverse gate aspects, Lilly suggests little visible ironwork.
preconditions: Moon weak light and adverse relevant aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not universal that weak Moon proves iron absent.

records.source_statement: Printed heading 'Are the Goods in the Owners hands' begins a separate possession check.
preconditions: Question of goods' owner custody, not thief dwelling.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Owner's hands is a source assertion, not measured ownership.

records.source_statement: Ascendant lord located in an angle is said to signify goods in owner's hands.
preconditions: Angular first-house lord.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is an authorial property-location claim.

records.source_statement: The planetary hour lord in an angle is a distinct rule predicting goods in owner's hands.
preconditions: Hour lord angular.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Must not replace hour lord with Moon-house lord.

records.source_statement: Moon's domicile ruler joined to hour lord in angle is said to mean owner has movables.
preconditions: Both Moon-house lord and hour lord together in an angle.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The 'moveable goods' claim differs from fixed goods below.

records.source_statement: Hour lord, Moon's term lord and second lord together angular with ascendant lord are alleged to put fixed goods in the owner's hands.
preconditions: The source names all four roles and angular meeting.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Fixed goods is not a fixed zodiac sign.

records.source_statement: If any of those listed lords is angular and in square, trine or sextile to the ascendant lord, Lilly forecasts owner recovering goods.
preconditions: Specified planetary lord in angle AND the named aspect to first lord.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Reacquisition differs from goods already being in owner's hands.

records.source_statement: First lord AND planetary hour lord in succedent house are said to place goods near the owner.
preconditions: Both first and hour lords in succedent houses.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not assume either one alone suffices.

records.source_statement: Moon OR its domicile lord in movable sign is said to show goods not far from owner.
preconditions: Printed uses lunar body or Moon house lord as alternatives.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No calibrated modern distance.

records.source_statement: Moon-term ruler OR second lord in succedent house is another near-owner indication.
preconditions: Specific ruler in succedent house.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from first+hour conjunction rule.

records.source_statement: The previously enumerated planet lords in cadent houses are said to show goods far from owner.
preconditions: Cadency of the named significator, not arbitrary planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Far has no exact geographic definition in this sentence.

records.source_statement: Printed heading 'Whether the Goods be in the custody of the Thiefe' begins a separate present-possession question.
preconditions: This concerns source-imagined custody, not thief identification.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keeps later ownership and recovery rules distinct.

records.source_statement: A presumed thief significator giving its planetary power to another planet is taken to mean goods are no longer kept by the thief.
preconditions: There must be a relevant transfer of power from the source's thief significator.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This does not identify the new possessor.

records.source_statement: When the presumed thief significator does not give power to another planet, Lilly says goods remain in its own power or custody.
preconditions: No transfer of power from thief significator.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is not independent evidence any theft occurred.

records.source_statement: The term lord of the thief significator is used to assert a change of the person's social estate.
preconditions: Identify term occupied by the designated thief significator.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source describes status, not confirmed criminal biography.

records.source_statement: An unfortunate planet in a fortunate term is said to describe a supposedly low-born thief who has risen into better circumstances.
preconditions: Malefic planet in a benefic term.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical class prejudice is not a valid person classification.

records.source_statement: A fortunate planet occupying the term of an infortune is said to indicate the reverse social movement.
preconditions: Benefic planet in an unfortunate term.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source's 'say the contrary' leaves the exact social change partially implicit.

records.source_statement: The distinct heading 'If he carried all with him' begins an account of how much property was allegedly taken.
preconditions: Heading precedes seventh/eighth lord placements.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: It is not a second observed theft event.

records.source_statement: Seventh lord angular is said to show a supposed thief intended to carry everything off but could not.
preconditions: The original seventh lord angular.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Intent is a speculative historical attribution, not evidence of motive.

records.source_statement: Seventh lord succedent and eighth lord strongly accompanying it is said to mean all goods were carried away.
preconditions: Both seventh lord succedent and eighth lord strong with it.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from seventh alone in angle.

records.source_statement: Both seventh and eighth lords cadent are interpreted as the suspected person not taking or keeping the goods.
preconditions: Both named lords cadent.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author's interpretation does not prove innocence.

records.source_statement: A heading 'The distance of the thing from the Owner' introduces several competing old distance scales.
preconditions: Original printed p350 before a separate 'How far ...' heading.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source itself notes country limitation of some rules.

records.source_statement: The distance between thief significator and Moon is counted by degrees; in fixed sign one degree allegedly equals one mile.
preconditions: Degree separation of named significators with fixed-sign modality.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This historical unit is not geographic validation.

records.source_statement: For common-sign classification, Lilly assigns tenths of a mile per degree in this particular method.
preconditions: The same angular separation but common-sign mode.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source's unusual 'so many tenths' wording needs original print fidelity.

records.source_statement: For movable-sign classification, Lilly assigns rods per degree, rather than miles.
preconditions: The same angular separation but movable mode.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The printed margin says these rules favour the country, not necessarily the town.

records.source_statement: Degrees separating seventh lord and hour lord are associated with thousands of paces to a fugitive.
preconditions: The named seventh and hour lords, not Moon/ascendant.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is an alternate fugitive-person distance method, not tested travel data.

records.source_statement: The angular gap between ascendant and its lord is used to conjecture distance from the original loss site to the thing.
preconditions: Ascendant point and its lord must be computed in question chart.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source gives this as another method, not necessarily compatible with others.

records.source_statement: The number of degrees the relevant significator has advanced into its zodiac sign is taken as miles from where cattle went missing; directional quarter comes from fourth lord.
preconditions: The source is discussing missing cattle and specific sign degree.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No verified distances or bearings.

records.source_statement: Separate printed heading 'How far the thing is from the Querent' introduces whole-sign distance reckoning.
preconditions: Not the same as earlier degrees-from-Moon method.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not merge distinct formula denominators.

records.source_statement: Count whole signs between ascendant and its lord; for that lord in fixed sign, Lilly assigns four miles per sign, with extra degrees added by its sign.
preconditions: Ascendant's lord and ascendant point, fixed sign; carries over to p351.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Continuation spans the original page break. This row had a shifted original draft schema; the exact prior source bytes were frozen before mechanical repair.
Editorial source paraphrase only; no independently authenticated person or outcome.

records.source_statement: In the same whole-sign scale, a common-sign first lord yields one and a half miles per sign.
preconditions: The ascendant lord is in common sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Continuation spans the original page break. This row had a shifted original draft schema; the exact prior source bytes were frozen before mechanical repair.
Editorial source paraphrase only; no independently authenticated person or outcome.

records.source_statement: In the same whole-sign scale, a movable-sign first lord yields half a mile per sign.
preconditions: The ascendant lord is in movable sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Continuation spans the original page break. This row had a shifted original draft schema; the exact prior source bytes were frozen before mechanical repair.
Editorial source paraphrase only; no independently authenticated person or outcome.

records.source_statement: The continued distance discussion says each sign separating the relevant significators receives a mileage value according to the sign occupied by the ascendant lord, with leftover degrees apportioned.
preconditions: The relevant two planets/significators, their angular separation and ascendant-lord sign class are identified.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The passage begins above PDF385; do not infer the entire distance method or apply it beyond this thief/lost-goods topic.

records.source_statement: In Lilly's printed example Saturn is in a fixed sign and the three intervening signs are valued at four miles each, totalling twelve miles.
preconditions: Example-specific Saturn/fixed-sign setup and three intervening signs.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is historical worked arithmetic, not measured distance.

records.source_statement: In the same example three additional degrees are assigned half a mile, producing twelve and a half miles in all.
preconditions: Use the example's source-chosen per-sign and partial-degree conventions.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The initial zodiac glyph and exact minute transcription must be source verified; do not back-calculate a general true-distance unit.

records.source_statement: A distinct source heading begins: The Place where the Goods stolne are.
preconditions: Begins after worked distance example.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Scope is identifying hypothetical hidden goods, not the criminal or recovery evidence.

records.source_statement: For stolen goods Lilly initially compares the sign held by the thief significator with the sign/place of the fourth-house ruler; agreement supports the place classification.
preconditions: Thief significator and fourth-house ruler must both be specified.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This presumes a thief under the historical question; not independent proof of theft.

records.source_statement: If thief's significator and fourth lord do not agree, Lilly gives greater place-classification weight to the fourth-house ruler.
preconditions: The two initial significations disagree.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a hierarchy, not additional independent votes.

records.source_statement: Fourth lord in a movable sign is said to place the missing item high from the ground.
preconditions: The fourth ruler is in a movable sign in the lost-goods question.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical location conjecture only.

records.source_statement: Fourth lord in a fixed sign is said to place the hidden item in the earth.
preconditions: Fourth ruler in fixed sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not infer a genuine buried object.

records.source_statement: Fourth lord in a common sign is said to put the thing under the eaves of a house.
preconditions: Fourth ruler in common/bicorporeal sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from a later p386 common-sign chamber-within-chamber claim; retain both.

records.source_statement: Besides fourth-house ruler Lilly uses the term of the sign in which the thief significator is placed to refine the location classification.
preconditions: The signifier's precise term ruler/portion is calculable.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source sign/glyph mappings are period-specific and do not establish real locations.

records.source_statement: A significator in Aries is associated with a place where small beasts such as sheep or hogs are kept.
preconditions: The named thief/lost-thing significator is in Aries.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinguish this sign from Taurus/oxen.

records.source_statement: A significator in Leo is associated with places of animals that bite, such as dogs.
preconditions: The designated source significator is in Leo.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is symbolic setting taxonomy, not actual dog presence.

records.source_statement: A significator in Sagittarius is associated with a stable of horses or large beasts that are ridden.
preconditions: Specific Sagittarius placement.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical place conjecture.

records.source_statement: The text associates Taurus, Virgo or Capricorn with places for large cattle such as oxen and kine.
preconditions: Relevant lost-item significator in one of the three named earth signs.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The text also offers finer differences for Virgo and Capricorn; keep source context.

records.source_statement: A narrower source clause associates Virgo or Capricorn with camels, mules, horses or asses and similar useful working beasts.
preconditions: The specified Virgo/Capricorn branch.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This can overlap the broader Taurus/Virgo/Capricorn cattle classification without making both independently true.

records.source_statement: The text separately associates Virgo with barns, under-ground or near-ground storage, granaries and corn.
preconditions: Virgo sign in the source classification.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep local distinctions between agricultural storage and beasts.

records.source_statement: Capricorn is separately associated with places where goats, sheep and hogs are kept.
preconditions: Capricorn sign as visually printed.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The same sign can have multiple source analogies; no site is identified.

records.source_statement: Gemini, Libra and Aquarius are associated with a house; Gemini specifically with its wall.
preconditions: Air-sign branch; individual sign needed for detailed room claim.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Does not prove an object is actually indoors.

records.source_statement: Within the air-sign place classification Libra is assigned a small house or closet.
preconditions: Libra as specified sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not confuse this with Gemini's wall or Aquarius's high doorway.

records.source_statement: The Aquarius source glyph is associated with a door above a gate or another elevated place.
preconditions: Aquarius sign in relevant scheme.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: An original printed astrological-symbol reading, not a measured floor height.

records.source_statement: Cancer, Scorpio or Pisces are assigned watery locations, such as near water, a pit or cistern.
preconditions: One of three water signs is the relevant source sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The three signs have finer distinctions.

records.source_statement: Scorpio specifically is said to signify uncleanness or places for casting foul water.
preconditions: Scorpio sign branch.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The paragraph ends at the original PDF385/386 page turn; keep continuity.

records.source_statement: The p385 watery place list concludes by assigning Pisces to a place that is always moist.
preconditions: Pisces as sign in the preceding list.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Printed p386 continuation before next heading.

records.source_statement: A separate source heading begins The place where the thing lost or stolne is hidden.
preconditions: This is a distinct editorial section from earlier Place where Goods are.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not count the same fourth-house sign list as independent recovery successes.

records.source_statement: The hidden-place subsection again compares thief significator and lord of fourth, favouring agreement and otherwise relying on fourth ruler.
preconditions: A question concerning hiding place, with both significators specified.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Variant of p385 rule; record textual repetition without multiplying empirical evidence.

records.source_statement: In the hidden-place variant fourth lord in movable sign indicates a high place.
preconditions: Fourth-house lord in movable sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not distinct verified historical case from p385.

records.source_statement: In this variant fixed sign signifies a place on the earth or ground.
preconditions: Fourth lord in fixed sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The previous page says 'in the Earth'; preserve printed variation.

records.source_statement: In this variant a common sign means a covered place.
preconditions: Fourth lord in common sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different original descriptor from p385 under eaves.

records.source_statement: The subsection adds reading Moon's own sign and whether Moon is in or near the ascendant or midheaven; the sign ascending with Moon supplies the place's form.
preconditions: Moon's place and angular condition must be known.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source is not a standalone Moon-only geographic technique.

records.source_statement: A separate heading Where the Goods are introduces an additional location procedure.
preconditions: Begins after the hiding-place paragraph.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not treat it as a new numbered chapter.

records.source_statement: Lilly says to inspect the second-house lord and its almuten (the planet with most dignity there) to locate the goods.
preconditions: An actual second-house cusp and dignities are computed.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original marginal note says these judgments are more properly by the lord of the second; retain that preference.

records.source_statement: If second and fourth rulers are in the same sign Lilly says the goods are where they are and the thief and stolen item are together.
preconditions: Both second and fourth house lords in one sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The second/4th co-location is historical astrological inference, not an authenticated thief or physical proximity.

records.source_statement: If those rulers are not together, Lilly says to judge by the fourth.
preconditions: Second and fourth rulers occupy different signs.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinct from first stage's thief-significator/fourth comparison; preserve subjects.

records.source_statement: Fourth lord in fixed sign is assigned goods in the earth or a house without an inner chamber.
preconditions: Specific fourth lord and fixed sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different form from p385 fixed earth only.

records.source_statement: Fourth lord in movable sign is assigned an upper chamber, loft or room above another.
preconditions: Fourth lord occupies movable sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original room description rather than generic high place.

records.source_statement: Fourth lord in common sign signifies a chamber within another chamber.
preconditions: Fourth ruler in common sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not confuse with p385 eaves or earlier covered-place variant.

records.source_statement: For lost goods Lilly classifies the sign as fire/east, earth/south, air/west or water/north.
preconditions: Relevant fourth-house or goods sign selected.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical directional symbolism, not a geolocated result.

records.source_statement: Moon's term ruler angular and in a movable sign is assigned an enclosure with corn or grass.
preconditions: The LORD of Moon's term must be angular and in movable sign; Moon alone does not meet premise.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Use of term lord is not equivalent to Moon's domicile ruler.

records.source_statement: Moon's term ruler succedent and in fixed sign points to woods, parks or enclosed land beside a highway.
preconditions: The term lord occupies a succedent house and fixed sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Could imply an outdoor place, conditional on BOTH house and sign.

records.source_statement: Moon's term ruler cadent and in a common sign is assigned common land or pasture/meadow belonging to many men.
preconditions: Cadent house and common sign combined.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not any cadent planet or a general legal property finding.

records.source_statement: Lilly quotes Haly's report of a lost-object question with LEO ascending; the sentence continues on printed p353 with Venus in the ascendant.
preconditions: Original PDF386/printed352: 'Haly saith, it was asked him one time when' plus Leo (♌) ascending; original PDF387/printed353: Venus (♀) therein.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a quoted historical source's self-report, not an independent outcome. Leo is the printed sign glyph; Libra was an editorial misreading. Do not attribute the episode directly to Lilly.

records.source_statement: In the continuation of Haly's historical Leo-ascending, Venus-in-first question, Haly says the lost object lay under a bed, near a robe or covering, attributing the bed symbolism to Venus.
preconditions: Leo (♌) rising and Venus (♀) within ascendant in the previous sentence; printed PDF386–387. The source explicitly attributes the report to Haly.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No chart, dated question, or independently authenticated lost-object retrieval was supplied. Do not credit this as Lilly's personal test or evidence of success.

records.source_statement: The heading Lost or stolen in what part of the house opens a more specific interior-location inquiry.
preconditions: The prior general goods-place methods have not all failed by default.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Another unnumbered source heading, not a separately observed loss.

records.source_statement: For the interior position Lilly tells the reader to inspect lord of fourth and the planet physically occupying fourth.
preconditions: Fourth-house ruler and occupant both need identification.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A planet elsewhere in the horoscope is not automatically applicable.

records.source_statement: Saturn as the relevant fourth-house planet is assigned a dark or abandoned place, privy/jakes, deep place or place seldom visited.
preconditions: Saturn must be relevant under the fourth-house planet/place instruction.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The content is descriptive historical analogy, not proof of location.

records.source_statement: Jupiter in the fourth-place context signifies wood, bushes or briars.
preconditions: Jupiter as the relevant planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: One of several arbitrary place classifications.

records.source_statement: Mars in the fourth-place context signifies a kitchen, near where fire is used, or a shop.
preconditions: Mars as relevant planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinguish kitchen/fire from Jupiter bush and Saturn jakes.

records.source_statement: Sun signifies a cloister, hall or seat/place of the master of the house.
preconditions: Sun as relevant fourth-house planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A historical owner/household relation.

records.source_statement: Venus signifies a woman's seat or bed, clothing, or where women commonly converse.
preconditions: Venus in relevant placement.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Gendered historical classification not diagnosis of a woman.

records.source_statement: Mercury signifies pictures, carving or books, or a place of corn, especially in Virgo.
preconditions: Mercury relevant and Virgo when applying the final narrower clause.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not collapse the Virgo condition into all Mercury readings.

records.source_statement: Moon signifies a pit, cistern or lavatory.
preconditions: Moon as relevant planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Moon-room analogy differs from its earlier generic lost-item sign.

records.source_statement: A new heading asks The forme or likenesse of the entring of the house.
preconditions: Applies to the opening/door location and internal house plan.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinct from actual placement of missing item.

records.source_statement: Sun's zodiacal place is said to describe the form and likeness of the opening of the house.
preconditions: Sun used as house-entry significator in this specific section.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different assignment than Moon/door position in PDF381.

records.source_statement: Moon signifies cellar, water-holding location or a pit below the house.
preconditions: Moon used as a house-structure indicator.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not equate Moon with only the door under this heading.

records.source_statement: Venus signifies a location for mirth, play and women.
preconditions: Venus in this source's house-entry classification.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical category, not actual observed household event.

records.source_statement: A printed lunar-node-like glyph is used for a high seat, stool, stair or ladder to climb.
preconditions: The source has a specific glyph in this passage.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Glyph identity to north/south node must be independently collated if ambiguous.

records.source_statement: The opposite node-like glyph is linked with stored wood, a beast shed or a pillar.
preconditions: The counterpart original source glyph.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not silently transpose node assignments.

records.source_statement: If Mercury is in a common sign Lilly expects a little cell inside another chamber.
preconditions: Mercury specifically in common sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Page387 wording pairs Mercury sign with room architecture.

records.source_statement: If Mercury is in a movable sign it signifies a little cell surrounded by another chamber.
preconditions: Mercury specifically in movable sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinguish from a doorway above ground.

records.source_statement: If Mercury is in a fixed sign Lilly says the house has no cellar or other chamber, comparing some country houses.
preconditions: Mercury specifically in fixed sign.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is not the identical fourth-ruler fixed sign rule from the preceding section.

records.source_statement: In the house-entry continuation Jupiter or Venus, one or both in the tenth house, signifies a fair opening to the door.
preconditions: Jupiter/Venus in tenth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinct from planets directly in fourth or a general benevolent planetary aspect.

records.source_statement: Saturn in tenth is said to mean the opening is near a ditch, pit or deep place.
preconditions: Saturn in tenth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source says door opening, not the stored goods themselves.

records.source_statement: Mars in tenth is said to place the entrance near making fire, slaughter/killing beasts, or heading them.
preconditions: Mars in tenth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Three historical examples; not a real fire or animal death.

records.source_statement: Mercury in tenth is said to mean the door opening near where the household master stores instruments or tools used around beasts.
preconditions: Mercury in tenth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Specific instrument-storage premise; not any written paper.

records.source_statement: Sun in tenth is associated with a stool, seat or bed near the entrance.
preconditions: Sun in tenth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source local architectural analogy only.

records.source_statement: For the Moon in the tenth, Lilly places the entryway near a door under the ground or another frequently used household feature, giving a furnace or a quern (hand grain mill) as examples.
preconditions: Moon in tenth in this printed house-entry subsection.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original PDF388/printed354 reads 'as a Furnace or Querne, or such like'; earlier editorial 'oven' was incorrect. Do not merge this with other Moon-based location sections.

records.source_statement: The heading asks what was stolen according to the lord of the second or tenth house.
preconditions: A stolen-goods question, with appointed house ruler.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Printed marginal note qualifies this as more properly decided by the SECOND lord.

records.source_statement: The first planetary inventory associates Saturn with lead, iron, azure/black/blue, wool, black garments, leather, heavy things and earth-working tools.
preconditions: Saturn identified as the relevant second (or heading's tenth) ruler.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original source materials list; not a verified inventory.

records.source_statement: The planetary inventory associates Jupiter with oil, honey, quinces, silk and silver.
preconditions: Jupiter is relevant goods-signifier in the heading's method.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not merge these with Jupiter-as-general-fortune inference.

records.source_statement: The inventory associates Venus with white clothes, white wine and green colour.
preconditions: Venus is relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Gendered material symbolism not empirical.

records.source_statement: Mars is linked to pepper, armour, weapons, red wine, red clothes, brass, war horses and hot items.
preconditions: Mars relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not interpret as evidence of weapon possession.

records.source_statement: Mercury is linked to books, pictures and implements or other associated goods.
preconditions: Mercury relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The later quality inventory additionally mentions money and paper; preserve separately.

records.source_statement: Sun is linked to gold, oranges, brass, carbuncles and yellow garments.
preconditions: Sun relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source material analogies, not an identified stolen object.

records.source_statement: Moon is linked with ordinary and common commodities.
preconditions: Moon relevant goods-signifier.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The next page continues with beast/animals and other categories.

records.source_statement: The heading The quality of the Goods stolne opens a separate second-lord classification.
preconditions: This is a duplicate thematic method with different items and explicit second-lord preference.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original margin says some judgments work more in countryside than city.

records.source_statement: With Saturn as second lord the source suggests lead, iron, kettle with three feet, black clothing, hide or animal skin.
preconditions: Saturn rules SECOND house specifically, not a planet anywhere in chart.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The original class includes material and artifact alternatives.

records.source_statement: With Jupiter as second lord Lilly suggests a white object such as tin, silver, variegated yellow/white or broadcloth.
preconditions: Jupiter as second-house ruler.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source's colour examples, not evidence the good was silver.

records.source_statement: With Sun as second lord the source suggests gold, precious things or other objects of good value.
preconditions: Sun as second-house ruler.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not necessarily identical list to first goods table.

records.source_statement: With Mars as second lord the source suggests fiery objects, swords, knives or weapons.
preconditions: Mars as second-house ruler.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No factual weapon identification.

records.source_statement: With Venus as second lord the source suggests things belonging to women: rings, fair garments, smocks, waistcoats or petticoats.
preconditions: Venus rules second.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical gendered object classification.

records.source_statement: With Moon as second lord the source suggests beasts: horses, mules, cows or poultry, especially in the country.
preconditions: Moon second-house lord; country/urban qualification from printed margin.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not infer animal health or actual theft of livestock.

records.source_statement: The goods-quality inventory continues with Mercury signifying money, books, paper, pictures and garments of various colours.
preconditions: Mercury as second-house ruler.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is continuation of printed p354 goods list; not a separate independent method.

records.source_statement: A separate heading A signe of recovery introduces a compressed list of supposedly excellent recovery configurations.
preconditions: The source labels the list as proven; no independent outcome records supplied.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A marginal instruction restricts the list to SIGNS OF SHORT ASCENSIONS.

records.source_statement: Moon in seventh trine to first lord is one of Lilly's listed recovery testimonies.
preconditions: Moon in seventh and trine to ascendant lord.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source does not say mere Moon in seventh always works.

records.source_statement: Venus or the second-house lord being in the ascendant is given as recovery testimony.
preconditions: Either Venus or lord2 is in first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source's punctuation warrants caution whether conjunction or separate alternatives.

records.source_statement: Jupiter in second, direct, is listed as a separate favourable recovery indicator.
preconditions: Jupiter is in second AND direct.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source's word direct is essential.

records.source_statement: Venus as lady of second in the ascendant appears as a more specific recovery testimony.
preconditions: Venus is ACTUALLY the second lord and in first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from Venus simply in first regardless of rulership.

records.source_statement: Moon in tenth trine to a planet occupying the second is included as a recovery sign.
preconditions: Moon physically tenth and trine to a planet physically second.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No arbitrary Moon-to-lord2 substitution.

records.source_statement: Moon in second trine to the second lord is separately listed.
preconditions: Moon in second; trine to lord2.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The paragraph lists alternatives, not a composite requiring the prior tenth configuration.

records.source_statement: Moon in second square Sun in twelfth is listed, somewhat unexpectedly, among the author's recovery testimonies.
preconditions: Moon in second and Sun in twelfth, square aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Don't silently repair this adverse-looking square into a trine.

records.source_statement: Ascendant lord physically in second is given as another recovery testimony.
preconditions: Ascendant lord in second.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a distinct named house position.

records.source_statement: Sun and Moon in trine are named as a recovery testimony.
preconditions: Specific solar-lunar trine.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No independent empirical support.

records.source_statement: Sun and Moon trine with the CUSP of second house is listed as an additional claim.
preconditions: Original source wording can be read as Sun and Moon both trining the cusp; verify exact syntax before automation.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not interchangeable with Moon trine the lord of second.

records.source_statement: Second lord in fourth OR in querent's house (ascendant) is the list's last position condition.
preconditions: Lord2 in fourth or first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original body names querent's house = first.

records.source_statement: Lilly's original marginal note says these otherwise praised recovery rules must be judged in SIGNS OF SHORT ASCENSIONS.
preconditions: Applies to preceding 'A signe of recovery' collection.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not claim all listed positive examples apply in all signs.

records.source_statement: Another separate heading If it shall be recovered introduces deeper Moon-term/house-lord procedures.
preconditions: A source question whether stolen substance returns.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep distinct from previous short-ascension proof list.

records.source_statement: Lilly calls the lord of the Moon's TERM the significator of the stolen substance to be recovered.
preconditions: Calculate Moon's exact term ruler for specified horoscope.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Moon's domicile ruler and its term ruler are separate bodies/roles.

records.source_statement: If Moon's term lord and Moon's domicile lord BOTH increase in motion and number and are free of infortunes, Lilly predicts goods recovered whole and nothing diminished.
preconditions: Both named lords, increase in BOTH motion and 'number', and absence of affliction.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is strong source claim, not measured completeness.

records.source_statement: Lilly instructs to examine the ruler of the planetary hour in the same manner as the Moon's term ruler.
preconditions: The house/hour lord calculation is available.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not treat this as independent evidence or silently replace Moon-term ruling.

records.source_statement: Application of first lord TO Moon's term lord OR TO second-house lord, OR relevant reverse application, is another recovery channel.
preconditions: Directed applying aspect between those named significators.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original enumerates alternatives; record direction and target.

records.source_statement: Moon applying to both of the relevant lords OR to her own domicile lord is another source recovery condition.
preconditions: Moon must be applying; original qualified 'them both' differs from one arbitrary planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep alternative and non-independence.

records.source_statement: Source adds a more complicated branch involving Sun applying to its own lord and the Moon diminished in light, with the Moon's term lord and relevant house lords also applying.
preconditions: The source's explicit diminished-Moon qualifier and signifier names need preserving.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Syntax is nested and source image may support more than one clause attachment; keep uncertain instead of broadening.

records.source_statement: The author says the recovery conclusions are especially strong when the relevant planet significator is in an angle or succedent house.
preconditions: Qualified recovery combinations already met; angularity/cadency additional.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not make angularity alone sufficient for recovery.

records.source_statement: Continuation says if the Moon's term/house ruler or second-house ruler applies to ascendant lord, the thing lost shall be recovered.
preconditions: One of the designated lost-thing significators applies to first lord.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This finishes sentence from p389; do not attribute it to all planets.

records.source_statement: Moon or first lord applying to ascendant, or either applying to second-house lord or Moon-term lord, is said to support recovery through diligent search.
preconditions: Specific applicant and target; original gives multiple alternative contacts.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: A claim of retrieval after inquiry/search is not actual verified recovery.

records.source_statement: When BOTH lunar-term ruler and Moon's domicile ruler diminish in motion or number the author predicts much of the property lost and not recoverable.
preconditions: Both distinct lunar rulers and diminution.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Contrasts with both increasing, which the author repeats just below.

records.source_statement: The page repeats that Moon-term and Moon-house rulers increasing in number and motion, safely apart from infortunes, predict complete restoration.
preconditions: Both named lords increasing and free from malefics.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: An editorial repetition of p389, not independently witnessed recovery.

records.source_statement: Under the recovery claim, the author says significators NOT cadent from angles imply soon recovery; if they are IN angles, recovery is described as moderate in time.
preconditions: Retain the unusual printed contrast between not-cadent and in-angles.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not silently standardize timing based on later astrology conventions.

records.source_statement: A new heading It what time it shall be recovered opens degree-to-time conversion.
preconditions: Requires earlier recovery significators and a perfecting aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Separate whether-recovered from how-soon procedure.

records.source_statement: Lilly instructs counting degrees between the TWO planets that signify the actual recovery, then translating degrees to hours, days, weeks or years.
preconditions: Two specific planets and directed application, not generic zodiac gap.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The mapping depends on where the planets are placed.

records.source_statement: Movable signs are said to require the shorter time, indicated in weeks or months.
preconditions: Both recovery significators / their applying configuration in the specified movable signs.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not extrapolate to fixed seven-day increment.

records.source_statement: Fixed signs are said to signify months or years until claimed recovery.
preconditions: Specified source sign category.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is not a calibrated modern time prediction.

records.source_statement: Common signs are assigned a time between the movable and fixed extremes.
preconditions: Common sign condition.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The text does not give exact number of months absent degrees and other conditions.

records.source_statement: A recovery significator quick in motion is said to hasten return.
preconditions: A specific relevant significator moving swiftly.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not the same as merely in movable sign.

records.source_statement: The source also describes significators falling from angles as shortening the delay before recovery.
preconditions: The planets that signify recovery are falling away from angles.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This can seem contrary to other angular rules and needs contextual preservation.

records.source_statement: Lilly warns his timing judgments here belong PROPERLY to this stolen-goods chapter and must not be applied indiscriminately to other inquiries.
preconditions: The immediate recovery-timing rules are being interpreted.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: An explicit scope restriction, not an optional aside.

records.source_statement: A separate heading Aphorismes concerning Recovery begins near the bottom of PDF390.
preconditions: The source changes from general timing procedure to an additional unnumbered list.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The opening printed sentence continues onto original PDF391.

records.source_statement: The first aphorism starts with eighth lord in ascendant or with ascendant lord, but its consequent appears on the following page.
preconditions: Heading and antecedent only visible on PDF390.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not invent the missing consequent or classify it as a full condition until PDF391 is read.

records.source_statement: The first recovery aphorism completes its p390 sentence: eighth lord in ascendant or joined to first lord signifies recovery of the theft.
preconditions: Eighth-house lord is actually in first or with lord1.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not interchangeable with lord2 placed in eighth (negative in next clause).

records.source_statement: Lord of second situated in eighth is explicitly said to deny recovery.
preconditions: Second-house lord in eighth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is a source contrast with eighth lord in first.

records.source_statement: Saturn, Mars or Dragon Tail is said to signify loss/division of the goods such that not everything is recovered.
preconditions: The exact preceding source scope for these bodies is incomplete; other clauses specify placement.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Retain uncertainty about whether the glyph's house is implied, rather than treat any Saturn as loss.

records.source_statement: Second lord in ascendant is given as a recovery sign.
preconditions: Lord2 in first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinct from first lord in second.

records.source_statement: Ascendant lord in second signifies eventual return after a long search.
preconditions: Lord1 in second.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The text expressly says after long search; don't call it prompt.

records.source_statement: If second house or its lord is hindered, Lilly says not all the missing goods will be found and recovered.
preconditions: Second house or ruler afflicted.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is partial recovery warning, not denial of all return.

records.source_statement: A nested clause says lord1 and Moon with Sun, tenth lord or Moon-house lord, or seventh lord with first lord/in good aspect, can suggest recovery.
preconditions: Use the text's exact named lords and conjunction/aspect configurations; conditions are alternatives.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source's coordination is ambiguous; do not convert to mandatory simultaneous joining of every planet.

records.source_statement: The same nested clause unusually mentions seventh lord in combustion, or tenth lord agreeing with Moon-house lord, as part of a probable finding.
preconditions: Maintain the actual lord7 combust alternative or l10/Moon-house-lord agreement.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source is only 'probable' and contains a syntax ambiguity; do not silently remove combust as negative.

records.source_statement: If both Sun and Moon are under the earth, the source says the object cannot be recovered.
preconditions: BOTH luminaries below horizon in the relevant chart.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Separate from passages where Sun/Moon in tenth (above) are positive.

records.source_statement: Sun and Moon together beholding ascendant are said to mean what seems lost cannot actually be lost.
preconditions: Sun WITH Moon and their aspect to first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This rhetorical claim is not independently verified.

records.source_statement: If the Moon or ascendant lord bodily applies to the planet denoting recovery, Lilly claims the stolen item will THEN be recovered; separate retrograde/direct application qualifiers address how soon.
preconditions: One of Moon or first-house lord applies bodily to the identified recovery planet, original printed p357.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The printed consequent explicitly predicts return, not timing alone; the retrograde/direct alternatives remain separate next records. No observed recovery is established.

records.source_statement: When such an application occurs through retrogradation, Lilly predicts sudden recovery.
preconditions: A recovery significator applying by retrogradation.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The direction of application matters; retrograde planets otherwise can indicate delay.

records.source_statement: When such an application is through direction/direct motion, Lilly says the good may be recovered before anyone looks for it.
preconditions: The printed alternative to retrograde application.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Counterintuitive distinction must be retained as authorial reading.

records.source_statement: Moon's term lord applying to the same term is listed as a timing testimony.
preconditions: Term ruler of the Moon and the Moon's term itself.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Applying to a *place* differs from planet-to-planet aspect.

records.source_statement: Moon's domicile ruler applying to its own house is listed as timing testimony.
preconditions: The planet is lord of Moon's house and applies to that house.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinct from source Moon-term lord condition.

records.source_statement: Lord of second applying to its own house is a listed timing testimony.
preconditions: Second-house ruler/its domicile specifically.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not simply lord2 in house.

records.source_statement: Any of the just-named Moon-term, Moon-house or second lords applying to the ascendant provides an additional timing indication.
preconditions: An identified one of those rulers applies to first cusp.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No inference from unrelated planet.

records.source_statement: The printed Part-of-Fortune-like symbol is examined for testimony with ascendant lord or Moon; mutual application is a recovery hope.
preconditions: Part of Fortune glyph and aspect to named lord/Moon.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source symbol identification and ancient part algorithm need separate astronomy validation.

records.source_statement: Lord of Part of Fortune applying to ascendant lord, second house, the Part's place or Moon is another sign of hope/timing.
preconditions: Must identify the LORD of Part of Fortune, not just the part's numeric longitude.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This sentence crosses into p392, not an independent observed event.

records.source_statement: Lilly counts degrees between the recovery planet and the angle it first approaches to estimate time of recovery.
preconditions: A preselected recovery significator, specific FIRST angle, and number of degrees.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Unverified time conversion; not elapsed calendar time without an ephemeris.

records.source_statement: Sun and Moon mutually beholding each other in angles are said to signify eventual recovery with labour and pain, and separately more than one alleged thief.
preconditions: Both lights in angles, with an aspect to each other.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The claim about more than one thief belongs to this parent angular-aspect clause, not specifically to its following trine qualifier.
These are historical authorial assertions, not observed recoveries or identified persons.

records.source_statement: Within the preceding angular Sun–Moon aspect condition, an additional trine between the luminaries is said to ease recovery.
preconditions: A Sun–Moon trine within the preceding angular luminary condition.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This trine qualifies difficulty of recovery only; the separate multiple-actor assertion already belongs to the parent angular-aspect record.

records.source_statement: Moon in ascendant together with any Fortune is given as positive recovery testimony.
preconditions: Moon physically in first AND a Fortune with it.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Needs separation from just Moon in first.

records.source_statement: Moon under Sun's rays (sub radiis) or combust in the ascendant is said to mean the missing object will not be recovered.
preconditions: Moon in first AND under beams/combust.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from another clause 'if it be' with pain and labour; grammatical antecedent ambiguous.

records.source_statement: One qualification states that, if recovery still occurs under the afflicted Moon scenario, it comes with much pain and labour.
preconditions: A source-positive circumstance despite adverse Moon status.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not force a binary impossibility where the printed 'if it be' permits difficulty.

records.source_statement: Both Sun and Moon in tenth are said to imply sudden recovery.
preconditions: Sun AND Moon in tenth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Exact source says sudden rather than merely favorable.

records.source_statement: If Sun and Moon are nearer ascendant than any other angle, the author predicts recovery with trouble, anxiety, strife, bloodshed or quarrelling.
preconditions: The two luminaries are nearer first than all other angles.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The adverse outcome is alleged, not evidence of violence.

records.source_statement: Sun in ascendant is given as recovery testimony EXCEPT when ascendant is Libra or Aquarius, where the Sun is called weak.
preconditions: Sun in first, chart ascendant sign; exclude Libra/Aquarius.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not omit two explicit exceptions.

records.source_statement: Moon in ascendant with Jupiter is another recovery claim.
preconditions: Both Moon and Jupiter together in first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source-specific positive, not generic any Moon aspect.

records.source_statement: A new printed heading 'Of the discovery of the thief, and recovery of the goods' introduces suspected culprit detection as distinct from object restitution.
preconditions: Section follows recovery aphorisms.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not use astrological reading as evidence of criminal guilt or to identify real people.

records.source_statement: Moon in ascendant OR Moon trining ascendant lord is said to locate the thief.
preconditions: Moon physically in first OR trine to first lord.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different return of goods versus identification of alleged thief.

records.source_statement: Trine between Sun and Moon is another return-of-goods indication in the discovery subsection.
preconditions: Luminaries trine one another.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No independent case.

records.source_statement: Sun and Moon joined to seventh lord or in aspect to him are said to prevent the suspected thief from hiding.
preconditions: Sun and Moon relevant to the seventh lord by conjunction/aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This presupposes a thief and offers no modern guilt proof.

records.source_statement: Lilly says if the lord of the ascendant applies to 'the second', or the lord of the second applies to 'the Ascendant', the goods are recovered. The original objects are not explicitly called the second and first house LORDS, respectively.
preconditions: Original PDF392/printed358 uses 'Lord of the Ascendant apply to the second, or the Lord of the second to the Ascendant'; preserve directional applications without replacing the literal objects.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The phrase may describe contacts with house cusps or planetary rulers; no definite lord1↔lord2 aspect is certified from this clause alone. The next clause separately uses eighth-house lord and second-house lord.

records.source_statement: Application or translation of light between eighth and second lords is another proposed recovery testimony.
preconditions: Lord8 and lord2 with an actual application or intermediary.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not an independent theft case.

records.source_statement: Eighth lord placed in second is also given as positive recovery testimony.
preconditions: Lord8 in house2.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from second lord in eighth (negative).

records.source_statement: Moon in second along with a Fortune is source-positive for recovering goods.
preconditions: Moon physically second, Fortune there.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source next specifies a separate good aspect to Moon's own house or lord.

records.source_statement: Moon in second applying by favourable aspect to its own domicile house or the ruler of the sign where it stands is given as recovery testimony.
preconditions: Moon in second AND specified favorable lunar aspect.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The original phrase might designate a zodiacal house PLACE or its LORD, kept distinct.

records.source_statement: Saturn, Mars or Dragon Tail in second is explicitly described as among chief no-recovery indications.
preconditions: Any of those named adverse bodies in house2.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Other conditions in same paragraph can override a generic positive placement.

records.source_statement: Second lord in eighth OR combust is likewise said to deny recovery.
preconditions: Lord2 in eighth or combust.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Alternative negative conditions, not both necessary.

records.source_statement: Second lord applying by ANY aspect to eighth lord is described here as a no-recovery condition.
preconditions: Lord2 applying to lord8.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This conflicts with preceding recovery claim of eighth/second light translation; preserve as separate source claim.

records.source_statement: The bottom of page392 begins a counter-condition: second lord in exaltation provides great hope of recovery, completed on PDF393.
preconditions: Second-house lord in exaltation; following context continues.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not stop at page392 and omit the following especially-if qualification.

records.source_statement: Continuation from previous page says second lord in exaltation gives great hope of recovery, particularly with additional good recovery testimony.
preconditions: Second lord in its exaltation AND any stated extra support.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not replace a conditional hope with certainty.

records.source_statement: A new source heading Of Theft introduces a separate list of alleged property-recovery and thief-related rules.
preconditions: Begins after the prior exaltation sentence.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Textual heading is original; nearby handwritten numbering is not a printed chapter number.

records.source_statement: Seventh lord in ascendant is claimed to mean the theft/goods shall be restored.
preconditions: Lord7 in first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is in the Of Theft subsection, not the later in-person capture inquiry.

records.source_statement: Ascendant lord in seventh is said to mean the lost goods will be found only after much inquiry.
preconditions: Lord1 in seventh.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Timing qualifier 'after much enquiry' essential.

records.source_statement: Moon in ascendant OR Moon with the ascendant lord is said to mean the stolen goods may be found.
preconditions: Moon in first or joined to lord1.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The original hedges 'shall or may'; not categorical.

records.source_statement: Moon in first WITH the ascendant lord is a more specific recovery claim.
preconditions: Both Moon and first lord occupy first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: May overlap the previous source alternatives, not an independent person/case.

records.source_statement: Sun and Moon in first, together with eighth lord and first lord in first, form a stronger source configuration predicting goods found.
preconditions: The printed clause may conjoin Sun/Moon in first and lord8 with lord1 in first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Nested source syntax unclear; retain rather than imposing one exact Boolean structure.

records.source_statement: Second lord in eighth again means the goods cannot be had.
preconditions: Lord2 occupies house8.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Repetition from earlier negative recovery passage.

records.source_statement: Saturn, Mars or Dragon Tail in second are said to mean the property will not be recovered.
preconditions: One named negative body in house2.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not infer any real theft.

records.source_statement: Lord2 in ascendant means the goods are recovered, but no one knows how.
preconditions: Lord2 in first.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Keep 'none shall know how' source claim.

records.source_statement: First lord in second is said to give recovery after great labour.
preconditions: Lord1 in house2.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Separately qualified delay/difficulty.

records.source_statement: Second lord cadent from an angle is said to deny recovery.
preconditions: Lord2 cadent.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The text juxtaposes a positive exaltation exception.

records.source_statement: Second lord in exaltation is said to make quick restoration, especially when Moon applies to that lord.
preconditions: Lord2 exalted; applying Moon strengthens time claim.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Different from a generic exalted planet.

records.source_statement: A heading Other Judgments of Thefts begins another set of source-tested rules.
preconditions: Original separate subsection after Of Theft.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not pool multiple similar rules as independent observed outcomes.

records.source_statement: First lord and seventh lord joined are said to mean the stolen good/thief is found through the querent's searching.
preconditions: Applying joining of the two relevant lords.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Lilly's subject is the thing sought under a theft question, not validated identification.

records.source_statement: First lord in seventh OR joined to lord8 OR seventh lord in ascendant are claimed to mean the thief returns of his own accord before going farther.
preconditions: One of three printed alternative configurations.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Lilly says he observed this often, but no independently authenticated cohort is provided.

records.source_statement: Moon separating from first lord and joining seventh lord is interpreted as the thief being found.
preconditions: Order: past separation from first THEN joining seventh.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not reverse with Moon separating seventh then joining first, which appears elsewhere.

records.source_statement: Seventh lord joined to an infortune IN AN ANGLE is said to mean the alleged thief will be taken.
preconditions: Lord7 conjunct infortune and angular.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinct from 'not taken' Fortune branch.

records.source_statement: Seventh lord joined to a Fortune is said not to be taken unless that Fortune is under Sun's beams or otherwise impeded.
preconditions: Lord7 with benefic and source exception (under beams/impeded).
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not claim a natural fortune absolutely prevents capture.

records.source_statement: If thief's seventh-house ruler goes toward combustion, source claims his death.
preconditions: Seventh lord applying to combustion.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Historical mortality claim is not modern forensic or medical evidence.

records.source_statement: Moon joined to an unfortunate planet is said to mean the thief will be found.
preconditions: Moon joined to infortune under source context.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Not proof any specific person is a thief.

records.source_statement: Moon joined to retrograde planet is said to mean alleged thief returns of his own accord.
preconditions: Moon joined to retrograde body.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The author claims he found this true, but does not provide blinded case records.

records.source_statement: Continuation states that if that planet is stationary, the thief does not move from his place until taken.
preconditions: The planet of the preceding Moon-to-retrograde comparison is stationary.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Distinguish stationary body from retrograde body and from geographical distance.

records.source_statement: A new heading Whether the Thief shall be knowne or not opens recognition rules.
preconditions: Scope is knowing/not knowing the alleged offender.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not use this to identify any real person.

records.source_statement: Lilly says the majority of planets occupying cadent houses indicates alleged thief will be known.
preconditions: MOST planets cadent, not one cadent planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Source makes strong inference with no evidence of detection.

records.source_statement: Sun in conjunction, square or opposition to the thief significator is claimed to make the thief known.
preconditions: Sun (☉) in conjunction (☌), square (□), or opposition (☍) to thief significator; the original p360 line4 has a same-volume errata entry.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Conjunction omitted from producer paraphrase; restored from original PDF394 line and p360/l4 errata. Exact editorial role of erratum remains uncertain; no claim of real thief identification.

records.source_statement: Sun sextile the thief's significator is said to make him suspected but not openly known.
preconditions: Source Sun-to-thief sextile as distinct from square/opposition.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No factual basis for suspecting people.

records.source_statement: A distinct heading Whether the Thief be suspected of the Owner or not introduces suspicion mechanics.
preconditions: Owner/suspect distinction.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Predictions about suspicion are not criminal truth.

records.source_statement: Thief significator square/opposition to first lord yields owner suspicion, whereas trine/sextile to first lord is said not to.
preconditions: Compare thief significator vs ascendant lord; aspect polarity.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: No independent measure of actual suspicion.

records.source_statement: Thief significator in conjunction with Moon is said to mean owner suspects a person in company with himself or using his company.
preconditions: Relevant thief significator bodily joined to Moon.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The statement concerns owner's belief, not culprit identity.

records.source_statement: Moon square/opposed to a planet in tenth or seventh is said to make owner suspect someone distant, unless the relevant house almuten aspects the Moon adversely.
preconditions: Moon hard aspect to planet in named house, plus exception.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: House-almuten exception and 'far' subject uncertain; preserve.

records.source_statement: Moon conjunct/square/opposed to a planet in seventh or its almuten is said to cause suspicion of that house's person.
preconditions: Moon's adverse aspect to occupant or almuten of seventh.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: This is owner's suspicion, not proof.

records.source_statement: If Moon instead aspects another planet, the owner is said to suspect that different person rather than the thief.
preconditions: Moon's actual aspect is to OTHER planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Useful negative distinction: suspected person may differ from culprit.

records.source_statement: If Moon is joined to or received by an evil planet, source identifies the suspected one with the alleged thief.
preconditions: Moon joined/received by an ill planet in author's interpretation.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not claim a particular person guilty based on Moon.

records.source_statement: Lilly asks reader to compare strength of first lord and Moon and any virtue received/separated from evil planets to decide who acted.
preconditions: Specific earlier ill-planet transfers to first or Moon.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The grammar and temporal direction are complex; retain source uncertainty.

records.source_statement: Ascendant lord angular applying or separating to a planet in cadent house is said to tell truth about the theft.
preconditions: First lord angular, and aspecting cadent planet.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The source uses 'truth is said of him'; not independent verification of honest testimony.

records.source_statement: Moon joined to an angular planet, especially in tenth, is offered as parallel truthfulness testimony.
preconditions: Moon actually conjunct planet angular.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not substitute ordinary Moon aspect to any tenth planet.

records.source_statement: A new heading Who did the Deed or Theft begins offender-classification by houses and luminary placements.
preconditions: Historical speculative attribution.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Must not be used for real accusation or identity inference.

records.source_statement: Ascendant lord in the second, sixth or seventh, OR second lord in ascendant, is claimed to implicate the owner himself in the source's offender-classification list.
preconditions: Original printed 'second, sixt or seventh': sixt denotes sixth house, NOT first house.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: The producer draft misread printed 'sixt' as 'first'. This historical criminal accusation rule is not valid forensic evidence.

records.source_statement: Sun and Moon in fourth are assigned alleged deed to father, mother or friend.
preconditions: Luminaries in fourth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Multiple alleged relation roles; no actual named culprit.

records.source_statement: Sun or Moon in fifth is associated with son or daughter of owner.
preconditions: Either Sun or Moon in fifth.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Do not combine fifth-lord mediation from other chapter.

records.source_statement: In Lilly's historical offender-role list, Sun OR Moon in the SIXTH house denotes a servant (not the first house).
preconditions: Sun OR Moon physically in the SIXTH house in the p360 'Who did the Deed or Theft' subsection.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Original PDF394/printed360 says 'in the sixt, a Servant'; the earlier producer 'first' was a source-transcription error. This is not forensic evidence.

records.source_statement: Sun or Moon in seventh is assigned a wife in the source relationship-classification list.
preconditions: Luminary in seventh.
exceptions_and_evidence_limits: Page395 continues with Sun-Moon mutual aspects and domestic acquaintance variants.
